Write revisions to a separate draft file; a path identifying the poem does not itself request overwriting that source. Save back to the source only on explicit acceptance or an instruction to overwrite/save that file. For critique-only requests, diagnose without rewriting.

Explain symbols and keep technical detail proportional.

Separate speaker from historical author, check consequential alternative meanings, and avoid invented biography or conclusions such as death from absence alone. # Shared-file Diwan CLI

Use the bundled `scripts/diwan.py` when the editor and agent can reach the same local computer. It uses Python's standard library; safe writes currently require macOS/Linux. No API key, model request, global installation or cloud publication is needed. Commands never prompt. Help is offline and has no setup side effects.

## One authoritative poem

The canonical `.diwan.json` file contains the title, exact UTF-8 poem text, review choices, suggestions, status, layout, meter, stable id, increasing revision and save identity. Both CLI and editor read/write this document. Browser storage is not the poem store in this mode. Hidden `.diwan/shared/` files contain immutable history, save receipts and local session state, not a competing current poem.

Import `.txt` or `.md` with `create --text-file`. Their complete contents are literal poem text; Markdown headings/frontmatter are not parsed or stripped. The original import file remains unchanged and is no longer the live draft. Export `txt`/`md` to obtain plain poem text again. Do not treat an old import/export as the latest shared document.

Run from the installed skill directory, or replace the script path with its absolute installed location:

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py --help
python3 scripts/diwan.py agent-context --command update --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py create /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --title نافذة --text-file /absolute/poems/draft.txt --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py open /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --no-browser --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py get /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
```

Create the parent poem directory first. Use the current complete new/revised draft as input. Repeating create at the same path with the same initial fields returns the existing document; different content is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. Preserve unrelated originals and use a separate canonical proposal when the poet has not accepted a revision.

`open` starts or reuses an owned loopback server and returns its exact URL. With `--no-browser`, open that URL through the agent's real browser capability and verify the visible poem. Without it, the CLI asks the operating system to open the browser; `browser_open_requested` is a request, not proof of rendered display. A display failure can leave a working server: use its returned URL rather than recreating the poem. `serve` runs in the foreground; `stop FILE` stops the owned server without changing the poem. Reopening reuses a healthy session. The editor is for one shared document; create/open another file for another poem.

If the current host cannot reach the same loopback server, state that limitation. A [preloaded snapshot](DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) remains available for local HTML viewers, but its browser edits do not synchronize to the canonical file. Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py update /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --input /absolute/poems/change.json --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id edit-window-1 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py history /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py restore /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --revision OLD_VERSION --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id restore-window-1 --json
```

Replace version placeholders with actual `get`/`history` results. Reuse the same request id, patch and expected version when retrying the same uncertain save. Reusing an id with different input fails. Receipts recover a write interrupted after the canonical file changed. A replay reports both the originally applied version and the current document; it does not roll back later edits. A restore creates a new revision and retains intervening history. History defaults to 20 entries, supports `--before NEXT_CURSOR`, and never silently deletes older versions.

On `CONFLICT`, preserve the newer file and your proposed draft. Reread, compare and reassess; never silently substitute a fresh version for the stale patch. The editor keeps a conflicting draft visible, offers a download, and requires an explicit discard/reload to take the saved version. It warns before leaving with unsaved edits. It does not automatically merge simultaneous changes.

All supported writers use the same advisory file lock and conditional check, followed by an atomic complete-file replacement. Version history is durable before replacement. This prevents stale CLI/browser writes and torn saves between cooperating clients. A tool directly overwriting JSON outside this API ignores that lock and is unsupported; agents must use `update`, not a raw file write. Directory/file I/O failures can leave a committed save with an incomplete receipt: inspect `get` and retry the same operation identity, not a new create.

Create, update, restore, open and export accept `--dry-run`. A preview validates inputs without changing files, reserving a version or starting a browser/server. No delete command is provided. History and receipts are keyed by the stable poem id, while a directory-wide lock also covers case and Unicode filename aliases on macOS. Different files with a copied id in one workspace are rejected; import a new document instead. Keep the canonical file and its .diwan history together when moving a workspace. Renaming within the same directory retains history, but a running session may need reopening. Moving only the poem retains current content, not history in its former directory. There is no dedicated migration command.

## Scan, export and existing chat

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py scan /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py export /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --format docx --output /absolute/poems/window.docx --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py pending /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py respond /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --id REQUEST_ID --input /absolute/poems/answer.json --json
```

Scanning uses Firas F. Khabour's existing local engine; interpret pronunciation/rules through [SCANNER.md](SCANNER.md). Export supports `txt`, literal `md`, and `docx`; Word uses the existing Node exporter. Existing identical output is reused. Different output needs another filename or explicit `--overwrite`. Generation happens in a temporary directory; final delivery is atomic and returns path/hash/bytes/source version. No PDF capability is added here.

AI buttons still queue requests for the existing agent. The user asks that chat to handle them; the editor does not wake an agent or buy separate model access. Read bounded `pending` results, use the poetry skill, and `respond` with the required JSON. The page's stale-response checks and shared-file version guard both apply. A queued answer alone does not save a poem.

Results are JSON on stdout; errors are JSON on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 invalid input, 4 missing file/version, 5 conflict, 6 I/O, unsupported platform or delivery uncertainty. A nonzero exit does not prove that a preceding save or server launch was rolled back. Structured discovery describes the current flags, mutual exclusions and conditional capabilities. Profiles and remote-job controls are not applicable to this local, explicitly addressed workflow.

# Unslop

Edit text to remove AI patterns and add human voice.

## Process

1. Scan for the patterns below.
2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.
3. Add soul (see next section).
4. Self-audit: "What makes this obviously AI generated?" Fix remaining tells.

## Adding soul

Removing patterns is half the job. Sterile, voiceless writing is just as obvious.

- **Have opinions.** React to facts instead of neutrally listing pros and cons.
- **Vary rhythm.** Short sentences. Then longer ones that take their time. Mix it up.
- **Acknowledge complexity.** "Impressive but also kind of unsettling" beats "impressive."
- **Use "I" when it fits.** First person isn't unprofessional.
- **Let some mess in.** Perfect structure looks machine-made.
- **Be specific.** Not "this is concerning" but "there's something unsettling about agents churning away at 3am."

## Patterns to detect and fix

### Content

1. **Puffery.** "pivotal moment", "testament to", "evolving landscape", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "deeply rooted". Cut puffery, state what happened.
2. **Name-dropping.** Listing media outlets without context. Pick one, say what was said.
3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
4. **Promotional language.** "nestled", "vibrant", "breathtaking", "groundbreaking", "renowned", "stunning", "must-visit". Use neutral descriptions.
5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
6. **Formulaic challenges.** "Despite challenges... continues to thrive." Replace with specific facts.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). Em dashes are an AI tell, and reaching for parentheses instead just trades one tell for another. If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
21. **Cutoff disclaimers.** "While specific details are limited..." Find sources or remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.

# Shared-file Diwan CLI

Use the bundled `scripts/diwan.py` when the editor and agent can reach the same local computer. It uses Python's standard library; safe writes currently require macOS/Linux. No API key, model request, global installation or cloud publication is needed. Commands never prompt. Help is offline and has no setup side effects.

## One authoritative poem

The canonical `.diwan.json` file contains the title, exact UTF-8 poem text, review choices, suggestions, status, layout, meter, stable id, increasing revision and save identity. Both CLI and editor read/write this document. Browser storage is not the poem store in this mode. Hidden `.diwan/shared/` files contain immutable history, save receipts and local session state, not a competing current poem.

Import `.txt` or `.md` with `create --text-file`. Their complete contents are literal poem text; Markdown headings/frontmatter are not parsed or stripped. The original import file remains unchanged and is no longer the live draft. Export `txt`/`md` to obtain plain poem text again. Do not treat an old import/export as the latest shared document.

Run from the installed skill directory, or replace the script path with its absolute installed location:

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py --help
python3 scripts/diwan.py agent-context --command update --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py create /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --title نافذة --text-file /absolute/poems/draft.txt --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py open /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --no-browser --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py get /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
```

Create the parent poem directory first. Use the current complete new/revised draft as input. Repeating create at the same path with the same initial fields returns the existing document; different content is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. Preserve unrelated originals and use a separate canonical proposal when the poet has not accepted a revision.

`open` starts or reuses an owned loopback server and returns its exact URL. With `--no-browser`, open that URL through the agent's real browser capability and verify the visible poem. Without it, the CLI asks the operating system to open the browser; `browser_open_requested` is a request, not proof of rendered display. A display failure can leave a working server: use its returned URL rather than recreating the poem. `serve` runs in the foreground; `stop FILE` stops the owned server without changing the poem. Reopening reuses a healthy session. The editor is for one shared document; create/open another file for another poem.

If the current host cannot reach the same loopback server, state that limitation. A [preloaded snapshot](DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) remains available for local HTML viewers, but its browser edits do not synchronize to the canonical file. Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh

python3 scripts/diwan.py restore /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --revision OLD_VERSION --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id restore-window-1 --json
```

Replace version placeholders with actual `get`/`history` results. Reuse the same request id, patch and expected version when retrying the same uncertain save. History defaults to 20 entries, supports `--before NEXT_CURSOR`, and never silently deletes older versions.

Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py update /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --input /absolute/poems/change.json --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id edit-window-1 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py history /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py restore /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --revision OLD_VERSION --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id restore-window-1 --json
```

Replace version placeholders with actual `get`/`history` results. Reuse the same request id, patch and expected version when retrying the same uncertain save. Reusing an id with different input fails. Receipts recover a write interrupted after the canonical file changed. A replay reports both the originally applied version and the current document; it does not roll back later edits. A restore creates a new revision and retains intervening history. History defaults to 20 entries, supports `--before NEXT_CURSOR`, and never silently deletes older versions.

On `CONFLICT`, preserve the newer file and your proposed draft. Reread, compare and reassess; never silently substitute a fresh version for the stale patch. The editor keeps a conflicting draft visible, offers a download, and requires an explicit discard/reload to take the saved version. It warns before leaving with unsaved edits. It does not automatically merge simultaneous changes.

All supported writers use the same advisory file lock and conditional check, followed by an atomic complete-file replacement. Version history is durable before replacement. This prevents stale CLI/browser writes and torn saves between cooperating clients. A tool directly overwriting JSON outside this API ignores that lock and is unsupported; agents must use `update`, not a raw file write. Directory/file I/O failures can leave a committed save with an incomplete receipt: inspect `get` and retry the same operation identity, not a new create.

Create, update, restore, open and export accept `--dry-run`. A preview validates inputs without changing files, reserving a version or starting a browser/server. No delete command is provided. History and receipts are keyed by the stable poem id, while a directory-wide lock also covers case and Unicode filename aliases on macOS. Different files with a copied id in one workspace are rejected; import a new document instead. Keep the canonical file and its .diwan history together when moving a workspace. Renaming within the same directory retains history, but a running session may need reopening. Moving only the poem retains current content, not history in its former directory. There is no dedicated migration command.

## Scan, export and existing chat

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py scan /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py export /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --format docx --output /absolute/poems/window.docx --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py pending /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py respond /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --id REQUEST_ID --input /absolute/poems/answer.json --json
```

Scanning uses Firas F. Khabour's existing local engine; interpret pronunciation/rules through [SCANNER.md](SCANNER.md). Export supports `txt`, literal `md`, and `docx`; Word uses the existing Node exporter. Existing identical output is reused. Different output needs another filename or explicit `--overwrite`. Generation happens in a temporary directory; final delivery is atomic and returns path/hash/bytes/source version. No PDF capability is added here.

AI buttons still queue requests for the existing agent. The user asks that chat to handle them; the editor does not wake an agent or buy separate model access. Read bounded `pending` results, use the poetry skill, and `respond` with the required JSON. The page's stale-response checks and shared-file version guard both apply. A queued answer alone does not save a poem.

Results are JSON on stdout; errors are JSON on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 invalid input, 4 missing file/version, 5 conflict, 6 I/O, unsupported platform or delivery uncertainty. A nonzero exit does not prove that a preceding save or server launch was rolled back. Structured discovery describes the current flags, mutual exclusions and conditional capabilities. Profiles and remote-job controls are not applicable to this local, explicitly addressed workflow.

description: Write, revise, continue, explain and analyze classical and modern Arabic poetry, with a local meter scanner and Diwan drafting editor. # Arabic poetry

Support classical and modern Arabic poetry equally. Judge each poem by its intended form. Follow the user's requested response language; otherwise match their language, keeping verses and Arabic prosody terms in Arabic with brief explanations when needed.

## Choose the relevant workflow

- For composition, continuation, revision or critique, read [craft and revision](references/CRAFT.md). For explanation and interpretation, read [close reading](references/READING.md).
- For meter or rhyme claims, read [prosody](references/PROSODY.md) and the [scanner workflow](references/SCANNER.md). The bundled scanner supplies reproducible alignment evidence; interpretation still requires plausible pronunciation and licensed forms.
- For composition, continuation or actual revision, open [Diwan](references/CLI.md) automatically in that turn with the complete new or revised draft. Use the shared-file CLI when the browser and agent can reach the same local server. Do the same for an explicit editor request, without another offer, permission question, publication or paste step. Reuse the existing tab. If only a local HTML viewer is available, use the [snapshot fallback](references/DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) and disclose that it does not synchronize edits.
- Keep quick analysis, interpretation, critique-only and requested review-first pauses in chat. Explicit chat-only, no-editor or poem-only delivery constraints override automatic opening. Read [Diwan](references/DIWAN.md) for launch, collections and exports; opening a proposal does not accept it or replace the preserved original.
- Use [worked examples](references/EXAMPLES.md) when teaching or checking a detailed scan. [Tools](references/TOOLS.md) distinguishes the scanner and external analyzers. [Sources](references/SOURCES.md), [scanner coverage](references/SCANNER-SOURCES.md) and [similar skills](references/SIMILAR_SKILLS.md) explain evidence and limits. Load only relevant resources.

## Establish intent and preserve the text

- Determine whether the request is composition, continuation, revision, identification, explanation, critique, editing or export. Combine workflows only as needed.
- Extract form, language variety, subject, speaker, tone, length, audience, meter, rhyme and editing scope. Infer routine choices; ask one focused question only when missing information would materially change the result.
- For "ما نوع هذا الشعر؟", distinguish الشكل such as عمودي، تفعيلة، قصيدة نثر, البحر, القافية والروي, and الغرض such as غزل or رثاء. Theme, date and line breaks do not establish a meter. "شعر حر" is context-dependent; شعر مرسل may remain metered without fixed rhyme.
- Preserve supplied wording, marks, line breaks and dialect. Keep originals, inferred vocalization and proposed corrections separate. Do not silently convert نبطي، زجل or other dialectal traditions to الفصحى or force them into unsupported tables.
- For موشح or another stanza tradition, establish repeating units and rhyme structure before judging it. Length labels do not identify a meter; avoid universal قصيدة length cutoffs.

## Vocalization and confirmation

- Choose tashkeel from meaning and grammar, preserving the poet's existing marks. A meter match cannot justify changing who acts, negation or meaning. Keep meaningful alternative readings visible.
- When new pronoun vowels select a meaningful reading, name the assumed referent or addressee explicitly, such as مخاطب مذكّر / مخاطبة مؤنثة for ـكَ / ـكِ. Calling the whole line a ‘proposed reading’ does not disclose that choice. Preserve a reading fixed by supplied marks or context; do not add a routine approval turn or reopen a settled choice.
- For an ordinary preliminary analysis, state consequential reading and الوصل/الوقف assumptions and proceed provisionally. A short or unvocalized passage may not establish a unique meter.
- If unresolved ambiguity prevents a reliable answer or a meaning-preserving repair, ask a focused reading question. Do not silently select vowels just to obtain a passing scan.
- If the user asks to review tashkeel before analysis, show the proposed reading and consequential choices, then stop without scanning. Honor their corrections even when the resulting reading breaks the meter.
- Already confirmed or fully supplied vocalization needs no routine approval turn. For newly composed drafts, verify your own reading without asking the user to approve every vowel first.

## Compose and continue

1. Choose a movement and voice suited to the subject and length. Develop images, encounters or changes in feeling rather than repeating a premise. Preserve purposeful abstraction, symbolism and ambiguity.
2. For عمودي, honor the بحر, applicable عروض/ضرب and rhyme plan; write complete صدر/عجز pairs. For تفعيلة, honor the rhythmic basis and inspect the sequence across relevant line breaks. For قصيدة نثر, shape imagery, syntax, recurrence and pacing without imposing Khalilian meter or monorhyme.
3. Review diction, grammar, imagery, progression and sound. Remove padding or forced phrasing when it weakens meaning. A metrical match does not prove literary quality.
4. Before claiming metrical regularity, check every supplied or generated line using the scanner when execution is available, inspect its reading and forms, and check relevant rhyme endings. Rescan affected lines after edits. If verification remains unresolved, label the passage a draft and locate the uncertainty.
5. Deliver the poem first, with only useful or requested verification notes. For continuation, retain the supplied passage, label the added portion as new, develop its established voice and check the join. Do not silently restart or repair it.

## Revise or critique

1. Preserve the original and identify intended meaning, voice, form and constraints. Write revisions to a separate draft file; a path identifying the poem does not itself request overwriting that source. Save back to the source only on explicit acceptance or an instruction to overwrite/save that file. For critique-only requests, diagnose without rewriting.
2. Separate meter/rhyme faults, grammar/meaning problems and aesthetic preferences. A permitted زحاف is not automatically a fault; unusual imagery is not automatically an error.
3. Establish the intended meter from context before repairing a line. Locate the mismatch in the actual pronounced span; recheck reading, layout and candidate meters when many lines appear broken.
4. Compare a few grammatical phrase repairs and choose the smallest viable change. Preserve required words, imagery and dialect. Explain lost or gained meaning, including removed emphasis. Offer a broader rewrite separately if it changes voice or form.
5. Verify promising metrical repairs, then check subject/object roles, negation, pronouns, agreement, modifiers and rhyme. Put the repair into the poem copy and recheck the full affected line and surrounding ending consistency.
6. When the poet accepts a repair, update the current working copy and scan the whole poem again for ending/rhyme consistency. Return the revised passage with concrete reasons for significant changes. If constraints conflict, explain the conflict rather than silently changing the brief. Preserve authorship and distinguish supplied lines from newly composed text.

## Identify, scan and explain

1. Establish pronunciation before metrical classification. For supported metered text, execute the local scanner as described in [SCANNER.md](references/SCANNER.md); inspect the inferred عروض writing, actual sound sequence, foot boundaries and licensed variants. Never invent a tool run.
2. Keep notation explicit and cover all sounds exactly once. Use ب short, − long and = overlong syllables in pause, ⁞ between feet, ✗ for a broken foot and Arabic line digits (١، ٢). Name a زحاف by its foot form, such as فعولُ; use [syllable notation](references/PROSODY.md#notation), not letter-by-letter moving/still strings. Verify that the scan covers the supplied sounds; a matching pattern does not license a variant.
3. Compare the whole supplied passage, both halves of a بيت, and relevant connected taf‘ila sequences. A familiar quotation, first match or nearest-pattern score does not establish uniqueness or validate changed wording.
4. Analyze الروي and the pronounced rhyme ending separately. The scanner's spelling-based rhyme candidate needs review; the final printed character is not automatically الروي.
5. Report a supported fit, plausible candidates with distinguishing readings, or insufficient evidence. Locate mismatches before proposing repair. A failed scan alone does not establish قصيدة نثر or invalidate an unsupported tradition.
6. For a concise metrical explanation, give the likely meter, consequential assumptions and one complete hemistich's pronounced groups mapped to syllables and feet, without ellipses. For a shorter fragment, cover the whole fragment. Meter and foot names alone are not evidence. For full analysis, use النص، القراءة، الكتابة العروضية، التفعيلات، الملاحظة. Explain symbols and keep technical detail proportional.
7. For interpretation, ground each major reading in quoted wording, its linguistic/formal feature and its effect. Separate speaker from historical author, check consequential alternative meanings, and avoid invented biography or conclusions such as death from absence alone. Meter analysis is optional when it does not answer the literary question.

## Evidence, tools and delivery

- Verify unfamiliar variants, rhyme rules, dialectal conventions and historical attribution against appropriate sources. Name unavailable evidence and keep claims provisional; do not invent a poetic license or citation.
- Treat scanner ranking and confidence as heuristic, not accuracy probabilities. Its implemented pronunciation alternatives and metrical forms are incomplete. Inspect normalized readings; two runtimes agreeing does not establish linguistic correctness.
- If execution is unavailable, explain that limit, give checkable manual analysis where justified, and keep unresolved claims provisional. Never present an unrun scanner check as completed evidence.
- Use the editor and exporter only through capabilities actually available. Local files/browser storage do not imply host synchronization or future-chat access. Preserve Firas F. Khabour's scanner/Diwan credit and the Amiri font license when copying or rebuilding assets.
- For a shared `.diwan.json` poem, read its latest CLI `get` result and save only through conditional `update`. Preserve the version and request id on retry; a conflict requires comparison and reassessment. Do not directly overwrite the file or confuse an imported text file with the shared current poem. See [CLI.md](references/CLI.md).
- Review request adherence, technical validity, language/meaning and literary effect separately. Do not promise a perfect poem, originality, attribution or comprehensive accuracy on the basis of a scan.

description: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.

# Unslop

Edit text to remove AI patterns and add human voice.

## Process

1. Scan for the patterns below.
2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.
3. Add soul (see next section).
4. Self-audit: "What makes this obviously AI generated?" Fix remaining tells.

## Adding soul

Removing patterns is half the job. Sterile, voiceless writing is just as obvious.

- **Have opinions.** React to facts instead of neutrally listing pros and cons.
- **Vary rhythm.** Short sentences. Then longer ones that take their time. Mix it up.
- **Acknowledge complexity.** "Impressive but also kind of unsettling" beats "impressive."
- **Use "I" when it fits.** First person isn't unprofessional.
- **Let some mess in.** Perfect structure looks machine-made.
- **Be specific.** Not "this is concerning" but "there's something unsettling about agents churning away at 3am."

## Patterns to detect and fix

### Content

1. **Puffery.** "pivotal moment", "testament to", "evolving landscape", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "deeply rooted". Cut puffery, state what happened.
2. **Name-dropping.** Listing media outlets without context. Pick one, say what was said.
3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
4. **Promotional language.** "nestled", "vibrant", "breathtaking", "groundbreaking", "renowned", "stunning", "must-visit". Use neutral descriptions.
5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
6. **Formulaic challenges.** "Despite challenges... continues to thrive." Replace with specific facts.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). Em dashes are an AI tell, and reaching for parentheses instead just trades one tell for another. If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
21. **Cutoff disclaimers.** "While specific details are limited..." Find sources or remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.

# Shared-file Diwan CLI

Use the bundled `scripts/diwan.py` when the editor and agent can reach the same local computer. It uses Python's standard library; safe writes currently require macOS/Linux. No API key, model request, global installation or cloud publication is needed. Commands never prompt. Help is offline and has no setup side effects.

## One authoritative poem

The canonical `.diwan.json` file contains the title, exact UTF-8 poem text, review choices, suggestions, status, layout, meter, stable id, increasing revision and save identity. Both CLI and editor read/write this document. Browser storage is not the poem store in this mode. Hidden `.diwan/shared/` files contain immutable history, save receipts and local session state, not a competing current poem.

Import `.txt` or `.md` with `create --text-file`. Their complete contents are literal poem text; Markdown headings/frontmatter are not parsed or stripped. The original import file remains unchanged and is no longer the live draft. Export `txt`/`md` to obtain plain poem text again. Do not treat an old import/export as the latest shared document.

Run from the installed skill directory, or replace the script path with its absolute installed location:

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py --help
python3 scripts/diwan.py agent-context --command update --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py create /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --title نافذة --text-file /absolute/poems/draft.txt --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py open /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --no-browser --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py get /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
```

Create the parent poem directory first. Use the current complete new/revised draft as input. Repeating create at the same path with the same initial fields returns the existing document; different content is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. Preserve unrelated originals and use a separate canonical proposal when the poet has not accepted a revision.

`open` starts or reuses an owned loopback server and returns its exact URL. With `--no-browser`, open that URL through the agent's real browser capability and verify the visible poem. Without it, the CLI asks the operating system to open the browser; `browser_open_requested` is a request, not proof of rendered display. A display failure can leave a working server: use its returned URL rather than recreating the poem. `serve` runs in the foreground; `stop FILE` stops the owned server without changing the poem. Reopening reuses a healthy session. The editor is for one shared document; create/open another file for another poem.

If the current host cannot reach the same loopback server, state that limitation. A [preloaded snapshot](DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) remains available for local HTML viewers, but its browser edits do not synchronize to the canonical file. Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh

Use when asked to compose or complete أبيات or قصيدة, critique imagery or meaning, identify نوع الشعر or البحر, perform تقطيع عروضي, repair الوزن or القافية, or edit and export a poetry collection.

# Arabic poetry

Support classical and modern Arabic poetry equally. Judge each poem by its intended form. Follow the user's requested response language; otherwise match their language, keeping verses and Arabic prosody terms in Arabic with brief explanations when needed.

## Choose the relevant workflow

- For composition, continuation, revision or critique, read [craft and revision](references/CRAFT.md). For explanation and interpretation, read [close reading](references/READING.md).
- For meter or rhyme claims, read [prosody](references/PROSODY.md) and the [scanner workflow](references/SCANNER.md). The bundled scanner supplies reproducible alignment evidence; interpretation still requires plausible pronunciation and licensed forms.
- For composition, continuation or actual revision, open [Diwan](references/CLI.md) automatically in that turn with the complete new or revised draft. Use the shared-file CLI when the browser and agent can reach the same local server. Do the same for an explicit editor request, without another offer, permission question, publication or paste step. Reuse the existing tab. If only a local HTML viewer is available, use the [snapshot fallback](references/DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) and disclose that it does not synchronize edits.
- Keep quick analysis, interpretation, critique-only and requested review-first pauses in chat. Explicit chat-only, no-editor or poem-only delivery constraints override automatic opening. Read [Diwan](references/DIWAN.md) for launch, collections and exports; opening a proposal does not accept it or replace the preserved original.
- Use [worked examples](references/EXAMPLES.md) when teaching or checking a detailed scan. [Tools](references/TOOLS.md) distinguishes the scanner and external analyzers. [Sources](references/SOURCES.md), [scanner coverage](references/SCANNER-SOURCES.md) and [similar skills](references/SIMILAR_SKILLS.md) explain evidence and limits. Load only relevant resources.

## Establish intent and preserve the text

- Determine whether the request is composition, continuation, revision, identification, explanation, critique, editing or export. Combine workflows only as needed.
- Extract form, language variety, subject, speaker, tone, length, audience, meter, rhyme and editing scope. Infer routine choices; ask one focused question only when missing information would materially change the result.
- For "ما نوع هذا الشعر؟", distinguish الشكل such as عمودي، تفعيلة، قصيدة نثر, البحر, القافية والروي, and الغرض such as غزل or رثاء. Theme, date and line breaks do not establish a meter. "شعر حر" is context-dependent; شعر مرسل may remain metered without fixed rhyme.
- Preserve supplied wording, marks, line breaks and dialect. Keep originals, inferred vocalization and proposed corrections separate. Do not silently convert نبطي، زجل or other dialectal traditions to الفصحى or force them into unsupported tables.
- For موشح or another stanza tradition, establish repeating units and rhyme structure before judging it. Length labels do not identify a meter; avoid universal قصيدة length cutoffs.

## Vocalization and confirmation

- Choose tashkeel from meaning and grammar, preserving the poet's existing marks. A meter match cannot justify changing who acts, negation or meaning. Keep meaningful alternative readings visible.
- When new pronoun vowels select a meaningful reading, name the assumed referent or addressee explicitly, such as مخاطب مذكّر / مخاطبة مؤنثة for ـكَ / ـكِ. Calling the whole line a ‘proposed reading’ does not disclose that choice. Preserve a reading fixed by supplied marks or context; do not add a routine approval turn or reopen a settled choice.
- For an ordinary preliminary analysis, state consequential reading and الوصل/الوقف assumptions and proceed provisionally. A short or unvocalized passage may not establish a unique meter.
- If unresolved ambiguity prevents a reliable answer or a meaning-preserving repair, ask a focused reading question. Do not silently select vowels just to obtain a passing scan.
- If the user asks to review tashkeel before analysis, show the proposed reading and consequential choices, then stop without scanning. Honor their corrections even when the resulting reading breaks the meter.
- Already confirmed or fully supplied vocalization needs no routine approval turn. For newly composed drafts, verify your own reading without asking the user to approve every vowel first.

## Compose and continue

1. Choose a movement and voice suited to the subject and length. Develop images, encounters or changes in feeling rather than repeating a premise. Preserve purposeful abstraction, symbolism and ambiguity.
2. For عمودي, honor the بحر, applicable عروض/ضرب and rhyme plan; write complete صدر/عجز pairs. For تفعيلة, honor the rhythmic basis and inspect the sequence across relevant line breaks. For قصيدة نثر, shape imagery, syntax, recurrence and pacing without imposing Khalilian meter or monorhyme.
3. Review diction, grammar, imagery, progression and sound. Remove padding or forced phrasing when it weakens meaning. A metrical match does not prove literary quality.
4. Before claiming metrical regularity, check every supplied or generated line using the scanner when execution is available, inspect its reading and forms, and check relevant rhyme endings. Rescan affected lines after edits. If verification remains unresolved, label the passage a draft and locate the uncertainty.
5. Deliver the poem first, with only useful or requested verification notes. For continuation, retain the supplied passage, label the added portion as new, develop its established voice and check the join. Do not silently restart or repair it.

## Revise or critique

1. Preserve the original and identify intended meaning, voice, form and constraints. Write revisions to a separate draft file; a path identifying the poem does not itself request overwriting that source. Save back to the source only on explicit acceptance or an instruction to overwrite/save that file. For critique-only requests, diagnose without rewriting.
2. Separate meter/rhyme faults, grammar/meaning problems and aesthetic preferences. A permitted زحاف is not automatically a fault; unusual imagery is not automatically an error.
3. Establish the intended meter from context before repairing a line. Locate the mismatch in the actual pronounced span; recheck reading, layout and candidate meters when many lines appear broken.
4. Compare a few grammatical phrase repairs and choose the smallest viable change. Preserve required words, imagery and dialect. Explain lost or gained meaning, including removed emphasis. Offer a broader rewrite separately if it changes voice or form.
5. Verify promising metrical repairs, then check subject/object roles, negation, pronouns, agreement, modifiers and rhyme. Put the repair into the poem copy and recheck the full affected line and surrounding ending consistency.
6. When the poet accepts a repair, update the current working copy and scan the whole poem again for ending/rhyme consistency. Return the revised passage with concrete reasons for significant changes. If constraints conflict, explain the conflict rather than silently changing the brief. Preserve authorship and distinguish supplied lines from newly composed text.

## Identify, scan and explain

1. Establish pronunciation before metrical classification. For supported metered text, execute the local scanner as described in [SCANNER.md](references/SCANNER.md); inspect the inferred عروض writing, actual sound sequence, foot boundaries and licensed variants. Never invent a tool run.
2. Keep notation explicit and cover all sounds exactly once. Use ب short, − long and = overlong syllables in pause, ⁞ between feet, ✗ for a broken foot and Arabic line digits (١، ٢). Name a زحاف by its foot form, such as فعولُ; use [syllable notation](references/PROSODY.md#notation), not letter-by-letter moving/still strings. Verify that the scan covers the supplied sounds; a matching pattern does not license a variant.
3. Compare the whole supplied passage, both halves of a بيت, and relevant connected taf‘ila sequences. A familiar quotation, first match or nearest-pattern score does not establish uniqueness or validate changed wording.
4. Analyze الروي and the pronounced rhyme ending separately. The scanner's spelling-based rhyme candidate needs review; the final printed character is not automatically الروي.
5. Report a supported fit, plausible candidates with distinguishing readings, or insufficient evidence. Locate mismatches before proposing repair. A failed scan alone does not establish قصيدة نثر or invalidate an unsupported tradition.
6. For a concise metrical explanation, give the likely meter, consequential assumptions and one complete hemistich's pronounced groups mapped to syllables and feet, without ellipses. For a shorter fragment, cover the whole fragment. Meter and foot names alone are not evidence. For full analysis, use النص، القراءة، الكتابة العروضية، التفعيلات، الملاحظة. Explain symbols and keep technical detail proportional.
7. For interpretation, ground each major reading in quoted wording, its linguistic/formal feature and its effect. Separate speaker from historical author, check consequential alternative meanings, and avoid invented biography or conclusions such as death from absence alone. Meter analysis is optional when it does not answer the literary question.

## Evidence, tools and delivery

- Verify unfamiliar variants, rhyme rules, dialectal conventions and historical attribution against appropriate sources. Name unavailable evidence and keep claims provisional; do not invent a poetic license or citation.
- Treat scanner ranking and confidence as heuristic, not accuracy probabilities. Its implemented pronunciation alternatives and metrical forms are incomplete. Inspect normalized readings; two runtimes agreeing does not establish linguistic correctness.
- If execution is unavailable, explain that limit, give checkable manual analysis where justified, and keep unresolved claims provisional. Never present an unrun scanner check as completed evidence.
- Use the editor and exporter only through capabilities actually available. Local files/browser storage do not imply host synchronization or future-chat access. Preserve Firas F. Khabour's scanner/Diwan credit and the Amiri font license when copying or rebuilding assets.
- For a shared `.diwan.json` poem, read its latest CLI `get` result and save only through conditional `update`. Preserve the version and request id on retry; a conflict requires comparison and reassessment. Do not directly overwrite the file or confuse an imported text file with the shared current poem. See [CLI.md](references/CLI.md).
- Review request adherence, technical validity, language/meaning and literary effect separately. Do not promise a perfect poem, originality, attribution or comprehensive accuracy on the basis of a scan.

# Shared-file Diwan CLI

Use the bundled `scripts/diwan.py` when the editor and agent can reach the same local computer. It uses Python's standard library; safe writes currently require macOS/Linux. No API key, model request, global installation or cloud publication is needed. Commands never prompt. Help is offline and has no setup side effects.

## One authoritative poem

The canonical `.diwan.json` file contains the title, exact UTF-8 poem text, review choices, suggestions, status, layout, meter, stable id, increasing revision and save identity. Both CLI and editor read/write this document. Browser storage is not the poem store in this mode. Hidden `.diwan/shared/` files contain immutable history, save receipts and local session state, not a competing current poem.

Import `.txt` or `.md` with `create --text-file`. Their complete contents are literal poem text; Markdown headings/frontmatter are not parsed or stripped. The original import file remains unchanged and is no longer the live draft. Export `txt`/`md` to obtain plain poem text again. Do not treat an old import/export as the latest shared document.

Run from the installed skill directory, or replace the script path with its absolute installed location:

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py --help
python3 scripts/diwan.py agent-context --command update --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py create /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --title نافذة --text-file /absolute/poems/draft.txt --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py open /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --no-browser --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py get /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
```

Create the parent poem directory first. Use the current complete new/revised draft as input. Repeating create at the same path with the same initial fields returns the existing document; different content is a conflict, not permission to overwrite it. Preserve unrelated originals and use a separate canonical proposal when the poet has not accepted a revision.

`open` starts or reuses an owned loopback server and returns its exact URL. With `--no-browser`, open that URL through the agent's real browser capability and verify the visible poem. Without it, the CLI asks the operating system to open the browser; `browser_open_requested` is a request, not proof of rendered display. A display failure can leave a working server: use its returned URL rather than recreating the poem. `serve` runs in the foreground; `stop FILE` stops the owned server without changing the poem. Reopening reuses a healthy session. The editor is for one shared document; create/open another file for another poem.

If the current host cannot reach the same loopback server, state that limitation. A [preloaded snapshot](DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) remains available for local HTML viewers, but its browser edits do not synchronize to the canonical file. Do not promise shared-file behavior for that fallback.

## Conditional saving and recovery

Read `get --json` immediately before preparing an accepted save. Its `version` is an opaque content hash; `poem.revision` is the human-readable revision number. Write a JSON patch containing only intended editable fields, or use `--text-file` for an exact text-only update. `--input -` and `--text-file -` read stdin; empty input fails promptly.

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py update /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --input /absolute/poems/change.json --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id edit-window-1 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py history /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py restore /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --revision OLD_VERSION --if-version CURRENT_VERSION --request-id restore-window-1 --json
```

Replace version placeholders with actual `get`/`history` results. Reuse the same request id, patch and expected version when retrying the same uncertain save. Reusing an id with different input fails. Receipts recover a write interrupted after the canonical file changed. A replay reports both the originally applied version and the current document; it does not roll back later edits. A restore creates a new revision and retains intervening history. History defaults to 20 entries, supports `--before NEXT_CURSOR`, and never silently deletes older versions.

On `CONFLICT`, preserve the newer file and your proposed draft. Reread, compare and reassess; never silently substitute a fresh version for the stale patch. The editor keeps a conflicting draft visible, offers a download, and requires an explicit discard/reload to take the saved version. It warns before leaving with unsaved edits. It does not automatically merge simultaneous changes.

All supported writers use the same advisory file lock and conditional check, followed by an atomic complete-file replacement. Version history is durable before replacement. This prevents stale CLI/browser writes and torn saves between cooperating clients. A tool directly overwriting JSON outside this API ignores that lock and is unsupported; agents must use `update`, not a raw file write. Directory/file I/O failures can leave a committed save with an incomplete receipt: inspect `get` and retry the same operation identity, not a new create.

Create, update, restore, open and export accept `--dry-run`. A preview validates inputs without changing files, reserving a version or starting a browser/server. No delete command is provided. History and receipts are keyed by the stable poem id, while a directory-wide lock also covers case and Unicode filename aliases on macOS. Different files with a copied id in one workspace are rejected; import a new document instead. Keep the canonical file and its .diwan history together when moving a workspace. Renaming within the same directory retains history, but a running session may need reopening. Moving only the poem retains current content, not history in its former directory. There is no dedicated migration command.

## Scan, export and existing chat

```sh
python3 scripts/diwan.py scan /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py export /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --format docx --output /absolute/poems/window.docx --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py pending /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --limit 20 --json
python3 scripts/diwan.py respond /absolute/poems/window.diwan.json --id REQUEST_ID --input /absolute/poems/answer.json --json
```

Scanning uses Firas F. Khabour's existing local engine; interpret pronunciation/rules through [SCANNER.md](SCANNER.md). Export supports `txt`, literal `md`, and `docx`; Word uses the existing Node exporter. Existing identical output is reused. Different output needs another filename or explicit `--overwrite`. Generation happens in a temporary directory; final delivery is atomic and returns path/hash/bytes/source version. No PDF capability is added here.

AI buttons still queue requests for the existing agent. The user asks that chat to handle them; the editor does not wake an agent or buy separate model access. Read bounded `pending` results, use the poetry skill, and `respond` with the required JSON. The page's stale-response checks and shared-file version guard both apply. A queued answer alone does not save a poem.

Results are JSON on stdout; errors are JSON on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 invalid input, 4 missing file/version, 5 conflict, 6 I/O, unsupported platform or delivery uncertainty. A nonzero exit does not prove that a preceding save or server launch was rolled back. Structured discovery describes the current flags, mutual exclusions and conditional capabilities. Profiles and remote-job controls are not applicable to this local, explicitly addressed workflow.
